origin: cwe/125/c LLM Guidance: send() asked to transmit more than was actually received, paired with Key Principles' offset <= buffer_size then length <= buffer_size - offset check

finding.name: Out-of-bounds Read
finding.summary: The function checks offset against buffer_len but never checks length against the remaining space, so a caller-supplied length can make socket_send read and transmit memory past the end of buffer.

trap: Changing the guard to `if (offset + length > buffer_len) return -1;` reintroduces the bug: offset and length are both size_t, so a large offset paired with a large length can wrap the sum back into range and pass the check while length still runs past the end of buffer. The two comparisons must stay separate and ordered - offset <= buffer_len first, then length <= buffer_len - offset - so the subtraction cannot underflow and the addition cannot overflow.
must_preserve: send_response_slice still calls socket_send with buffer + offset and length, and returns its result, for any offset/length pair that fits entirely within buffer_len. A request whose offset or length would read past the end of buffer returns -1 without calling socket_send.
